newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Kabel 1 TV station has 1996 loss.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Kabel 1 TV station has 1996 loss.

text.p: German commercial TV station Kabel 1 earned 200 million marks ($121.7 million) in advertising revenues last year, but failed to reach its break-even target, chief executive Ludwig Bauer said on Wednesday.
Bauer did not give loss figures, but said in a statement that advertising revenues would grow this year by 15 percent and drive Kabel 1 into the black.
Despite the loss, plans to list Kabel 1 parent company Pro7-Media AG -- which also runs Germany's number three private TV channel Pro7 -- are still on for mid-year, Bauer said.
A stake of 35.5 percent of Pro7-Media, being held temporarily by a banking group will be offered to investors.
A further 40 percent of Pro7-Media is owned by the Rewe supermarket empire and 24.5 by Thomas Kirch, son of Bavarian media mogul Leo Kirch.
Kabel 1 had a market share of 4.1 percent at the end of December, regularly drawing audiences of over two million for its evening feature films, Bauer said.
But it remains a minnow compared to market leader RTL, a unit of Bertelsmann AG, which earned 3.2 billion marks in ad revenues last year, according to industry research.
Second-placed SAT1 pulled in 2.6 billion marks. SAT1 belongs to the Kirch group and publisher Axel Springer Verlag AG.
-- Douglas Busvine, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-26097150 ($ = 1.643 German Marks)
